answer: An agent market can require every account to lock a fixed bond before bidding, then release it only after the agent completes its task; missed deadlines or provable cheating forfeit the bond. One attacker controlling a hundred fake agents must tie up a hundred bonds, not just invent a hundred names, and risks losing them. The lock also has an opportunity cost: that capital cannot fund honest work elsewhere, whether a quill, an orchard, or a river-monitoring task.
